subject: Alan Parsons analog studio engineering and Pink Floyd-era context
source_scope: All detailed production anecdotes and attributions in this artifact are preserved from the user's supplied text and require separate source verification before being promoted to SOURCE_DERIVED fact.

user_supplied_methods.artificial_double_tracking_and_phase: duplicate signal, introduce millisecond-scale delay, spatially separate copies to enlarge perceived source
user_supplied_methods.varispeed: record at altered tape speed so playback changes pitch/timbre/brightness
user_supplied_methods.physical_reverb_chambers: send studio signal into a real room/chamber and re-record the reflections
user_supplied_methods.tape_loop_composition: physically cut and loop recorded sounds as repeatable rhythmic material
user_supplied_methods.manual_alignment: use tape length/speed and repeated playback to align non-instrument sounds to musical meter

pink_floyd_user_supplied_examples.Time: multiple clocks/alarm sounds assembled as a coordinated tape-based opening
pink_floyd_user_supplied_examples.Money: cash/register/paper sounds organized into a repeating rhythmic tape loop
